contract.json_path: flat for the core update fields (projectId, report_type, report_timeframe, report_creation_mode, grain, title, description all top-level body keys, matching create). Filter/schedule json_path fields (report_filters.*, dynamic_filters.test_run, mail_to.users/external_mails, frequency_details.time/day) were declared but not exercised in this probe — the report's report_filters was already {} before and after, and no scheduling/recipient fields were sent.

notes: PUT-vs-PATCH verdict: a true single-field PATCH is not reachable at all on this endpoint. Two independent enforcement layers force a near-complete resend: (1) the MCP tool client-side rejects any call missing the schema's declared-required fields (report_type, report_timeframe, report_creation_mode, projectId) before a request is even sent (attempt 1); (2) the live server additionally 422s if `title` is omitted (attempt 2) — 'name name is required' — even though `title` is NOT marked required in the declared schema. This directly contradicts the schema's own guidance text for `title` ('Written unconditionally — omit it and the title is set to null'): live, omitting title never reaches a silent-null outcome, it hard-fails 422 first. So the documented 'full replace nulls what you omit' behavior is only half right for title — in practice you cannot omit it at all, so it can never be silently nulled the way the docs describe. Once title/report_type/report_timeframe/report_creation_mode/projectId/grain were all resent at their persisted values and only `description` was changed, the call succeeded (attempt 3, 200) and the read-back (get_report_detail) confirmed description changed and title/report_type/report_timeframe/report_creation_mode/grain all survived unchanged — as expected, since we resent them ourselves, not because the endpoint merged. `is_dynamic` was deliberately omitted from the body in attempts 2 and 3 to test the same claim for a non-required field; it came back `false` in both the write response and the read-back, identical to its pre-update persisted value — this is INCONCLUSIVE for merge-vs-null (false-if-nulled and false-if-preserved are indistinguishable here) and is explicitly left unverified rather than guessed. Net assessment: this endpoint behaves less like a forgiving PATCH and more like a gated full-replace — most identity/type fields are protected from accidental omission by hard validation (client-side or 422), which is safer than silent data loss, but it also means the schema's stated 'omit-to-null' contract is not what actually happens for at least `title`. INHERITED-DRIFT CONFIRMED, SAME SERIALIZER: exactly the same declared-missing field (data.mail_to — required in the schema, absent from the actual response, both on create and here) and exactly the same 7 undeclared fields (data.updated_at, data.project_ids, data.included_projects, data.is_dynamic, data.grain, data.slack_notification, data.slack_notification_supported) came back on this update as were found on create_report for the same report id 10393. This is strong evidence create_report and update_report share one serializer rather than being two independently-drifted response shapes — the 'two representations of project (project_id vs project_ids/included_projects)' pattern is identical on both, matching the pattern already confirmed for projects elsewhere. STATUS CODE: update correctly returns 200 (not the 200-for-201 anomaly seen on create — that was specific to record creation, not reproduced here since this is a genuine update of an existing record). NO EMAIL SENT / SCHEDULING UNTOUCHED: frequency, frequency_details, users, external_mails were never included in any attempt. Baseline and post-update reads both show frequency=null, frequency_details=null, next_run_at=null, and no mail_to key at all — the report remains unscheduled exactly as it was created, and no recipient fields were populated or exercised. SC-489/SC-490/SC-491 (ids 10374/10390/10391) were never read or touched by this probe — only report 10393/SC-492 was used, per instructions.
